page.notes: Hebrew words in lines 3, 4, 9, 10, 12 and 14 are printed in a small, heavy face and are partly blurred; the letters are as far as I can make them out, and those marked [?] are doubtful. The numeral before "391" on the line after "Numeros" is a special symbol (ʒ), not clearly a Latin or Hebrew figure. The 2527 in line 3 is copied as printed. The "s" in "esta-" (line 22) is printed as a long-s-like form and is copied as printed. Ink smudges to the right of the text are not printed text and are left out.
